known_issues: Audio HAL lockup, Bluetooth/USB-C routing stuck, or OS mic conflict (Poco F3): If CIT passes hardware loopback in Safe Mode, clear Google app cache/microphone permission, reset audio settings, or reflash matching stock firmware/persist image before opening the chassis.

Main-to-sub-board interconnect flex cable or bottom charging sub-board fault: Clean and reseat the B2B flex connectors; if corrosion or pin damage is present, replace the charging sub-board and main interconnect flex cable with a known-good assembly.

Audio Codec / Smart Amplifier BGA dry joint or shorted rail: Clear any shorted decoupling capacitors on codec supply lines; if rails measure clean without shorts, flux and reball or replace the audio codec IC and verify speaker amp continuity.

SoC / CPU BGA cracked solder joints causing simultaneous audio & mic bus dropout: Lift the stacked RAM and SoC/CPU, wick and clean oxidized pads under the microscope, reball CPU and RAM using fresh leaded solder paste/stencil, and re-seat cleanly.

profile.verdict: On Xiaomi Poco F3 (Redmi K40, Mi 11X), simultaneous loss of microphone and sound is usually either a lower sub-board/flex disconnect, an audio codec/rail failure, or cracked BGA joints under the SoC. Always isolate software (CIT *#*#6484#*#*) and the bottom flex before applying hot air to the mainboard.
profile.overview:
Diagnostic dossier for Xiaomi Poco F3 (platform siblings: Redmi K40, Mi 11X) addressing no sound and microphone not working.

All findings below link directly to fetched external evidence (Wikipedia, iFixit, repair forums, and technician videos) and remain tagged as agent_draft until reviewed by a human technician.

failure_modes.title: Audio HAL lockup, Bluetooth/USB-C routing stuck, or OS mic conflict (Poco F3)
symptoms: Neither loudspeaker media audio nor primary microphone works until reboot (or fails after MIUI/HyperOS update)
Earphones/Bluetooth state may appear stuck, muting onboard earpiece/speaker and bottom mic
Voice recorder or dialer hangs when attempting to initialize audio stream
failure_modes.mechanism: On Qualcomm/Xiaomi devices, an audio HAL deadlock, stuck USB-C/headset detection, or background hotword listener seizing the audio stream prevents both mic capture and speaker output without an actual board short.
diagnose: Disable Bluetooth completely and check the status bar for phantom wired headset icons.
Open the built-in hardware test (CIT: dial *#*#6484#*#* or tap Kernel Version in Settings) and run Receiver, Speaker, Main Mic, and Top Mic tests separately.
Boot into Safe Mode or revoke microphone permission from the Google app and test Voice Recorder after a clean restart.
failure_modes.fix: If CIT passes hardware loopback in Safe Mode, clear Google app cache/microphone permission, reset audio settings, or reflash matching stock firmware/persist image before opening the chassis.
failure_modes.risk: Do not flash mismatched region firmware or wipe persist partitions without backing up calibration files.

failure_modes.title: Main-to-sub-board interconnect flex cable or bottom charging sub-board fault
symptoms: Bottom primary microphone dead on standard calls while loudspeaker or top mic may also cut out
Fault starts after a drop, chassis flex, or moisture near the USB-C port
Intermittent audio or mic dropout when pressing near the bottom half of the back cover
failure_modes.mechanism: The primary voice mic and bottom loudspeaker routes travel through the lower charging sub-board and the main-to-sub flex ribbon. A cracked solder ball under the B2B connector, corroded sub-board pad, or torn flex trace can pull down shared bias or SoundWire/speaker lines.
diagnose: Disconnect the battery first, then disconnect the main-to-sub-board flex cable at the mainboard B2B connector.
Test whether the top earpiece/speaker and top secondary microphone recover with the lower sub-board isolated.
Inspect both ends of the flex connector under a microscope for bent pins, corrosion, or micro-cracks.
failure_modes.fix: Clean and reseat the B2B flex connectors; if corrosion or pin damage is present, replace the charging sub-board and main interconnect flex cable with a known-good assembly.
failure_modes.risk: Always isolate the battery connector before unplugging or probing board-to-board flex cables to avoid blowing bias or power lines.

failure_modes.title: Audio Codec / Smart Amplifier BGA dry joint or shorted rail
symptoms: Both microphone input and speaker/earpiece output fail completely in CIT hardware diagnostics
Sub-board and flex replacement did not restore sound or mic
Recorder app freezes or returns audio hardware error immediately
failure_modes.mechanism: The discrete audio codec and smart speaker amplifiers handle ADC/DAC conversion for mics and speaker amplification over I2S/SoundWire and PMIC LDO rails. Drop impact or liquid ingress under the shield fractures BGA joints or shorts decoupling capacitors on codec supply rails.
diagnose: Remove the mainboard shield covering the audio codec and PMIC area and inspect under a microscope for liquid corrosion or cracked underfill.
Check decoupling capacitors surrounding the audio codec and smart amp in diode mode / resistance for shorts to ground before powering.
Verify codec clock, SoundWire/I2C control continuity, and LDO bias rails while attempting audio playback/recording.
failure_modes.fix: Clear any shorted decoupling capacitors on codec supply lines; if rails measure clean without shorts, flux and reball or replace the audio codec IC and verify speaker amp continuity.
failure_modes.risk: Excessive hot air near shielded/underfilled Qualcomm ICs can float adjacent PMIC or CPU solder balls. Pre-heat evenly and shield surrounding BGA packages.

failure_modes.title: SoC / CPU BGA cracked solder joints causing simultaneous audio & mic bus dropout
symptoms: Sudden simultaneous loss of speaker sound and both microphones (often after heating/gaming or a drop)
Audio or mic briefly returns when pressing gently on the CPU shield or flexing the board
Device may also exhibit intermittent freezes, camera errors, or reboots before going dead
failure_modes.mechanism: On Poco F3 / Redmi K40 / Mi 11X, thermal cycling and board flex fatigue the lead-free BGA solder balls under the stacked SoC/RAM. Because digital audio buses (SoundWire/I2S/Slimbus) route directly from the SoC, cracked balls sever both audio output and microphone paths simultaneously.
diagnose: Rule out software (CIT + Safe Mode), sub-board flex, and codec supply shorts first.
Perform a careful mechanical pressure check (non-conductive spudger gentle pressure over the CPU area during audio test) — temporary restoration confirms cracked CPU BGA balls.
Check diode mode on I2S/SoundWire/I2C lines between the audio codec pads and CPU when codec IC is lifted.
failure_modes.fix: Lift the stacked RAM and SoC/CPU, wick and clean oxidized pads under the microscope, reball CPU and RAM using fresh leaded solder paste/stencil, and re-seat cleanly.
failure_modes.risk: High-risk micro-soldering: stacked PoP RAM/CPU can delaminate, pop, or tear pads if underfill is not cleared and temperature profile is uncontrolled. Back up customer data before board heat if the phone still boots.

checks.label: CIT Hardware Menu isolation (*#*#6484#*#*)
checks.expect: Tests Main Mic, Top Mic, Earpiece, and Loudspeaker independently of dialer/third-party apps.

checks.label: Sub-board & interconnect flex isolation
checks.expect: Disconnecting the lower sub-board flex separates a shorted bottom mic/USB board from a mainboard audio codec or CPU fault.

checks.label: Codec & PMIC supply capacitor short check
checks.expect: No 0.000V dead shorts on filter caps around the audio codec and smart amp rails; compare against a known-good reference board before reballing.

checks.label: SoC BGA joint integrity test (after ruling out flex & codec)
checks.expect: If light pressure on the SoC briefly restores audio or mic, CPU/RAM BGA reballing is required rather than replacing speakers or mics.

parts.note: Low-cost first swap when B2B pins or flex traces are fatigued.

parts.note: Houses the primary bottom microphone and USB-C port.

parts.note: Replace or reball when codec lines are open/shorted or audio fails after sub-board isolation.

parts.note: Required if BGA solder fatigue under the SoC is confirmed.
